transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, good to meet you too. Um… I guess what finally pushed me to come in is I’ve been making these small mistakes that are kind of embarrassing. Like, I’ll turn in applications or research notes and then realize there’s a skipped question, or I mislabeled an artwork date—things I really thought I had checked.

It’s not like I’m trying to be careless, and I know everyone makes mistakes sometimes, but it’s happened enough that I started worrying it’s more than just normal slip-ups, if that makes sense.
Do you often have trouble sustaining your attention on tasks, even when you want to focus?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to overstate it, because sometimes I can get things done, but if I’m reading or writing at my desk, it doesn’t take much to pull me off track. Like a siren outside, or someone talking in the hallway, or even just a random thought about an exhibit idea.

And then I’ll sort of follow that without meaning to, and suddenly it’s been, like, twenty minutes before I realize I stopped working. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Looking back, were you having this same kind of trouble paying attention when you were a child?

Yeah… I think there were signs, though I didn’t really think of it that way at the time. In elementary school my teachers would usually say nice things, like that I had good ideas, so it wasn’t like I was, um, trying not to do the work.

But they’d also write comments about me forgetting to turn in worksheets, or losing the instructions, or missing small details. My parents had to check my backpack pretty much every night or I’d overlook something. I don’t know if that counts as the same kind of attention problem, but it does sound kind of similar now that I’m saying it.
When you’re trying to work, do you often find that worry is what pulls your attention away?

Um… I’m not sure it’s usually worry, exactly. I mean, I do worry sometimes, like anyone, but when I get pulled away from work it doesn’t always feel like I’m sitting there anxious about something.

It’s more like my attention just kind of… slips? But maybe I’m not describing it well. Do you mean worry as in feeling anxious, or more like just thinking about things I need to do?
Do you often avoid or put off tasks that require sustained mental effort, like reading, paperwork, or detailed writing?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to, but I think I do. If I know something is going to take a lot of concentration, like drafting a curatorial proposal or reading a really dense theory chapter, I’ll kind of… do everything around it first.

Like smaller errands, organizing things, answering easier messages — stuff that feels productive, so it doesn’t feel like I’m just avoiding it. But then suddenly it’s the night before it’s due and I’m finally doing the actual thing. I don’t know if that’s what you mean by putting it off, but… yeah, that happens.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking your work over and over because you’re afraid you might have made a mistake?

Um… I don’t think so? Not over and over, really.

I’ll reread something if it’s important, or if I’m not sure it makes sense, but it’s not usually because I’m scared I made a mistake. It’s more just… normal checking, I think. Unless I’m missing what you mean by “repeatedly”?
Have these attention and organization problems caused real difficulties for you at work or school?

Yeah… I think it has, unfortunately. Not in a total disaster kind of way, but enough that it’s been noticeable.

I’ve turned in work late, and I’ve missed a couple application deadlines that I really shouldn’t have missed. And one of my mentors basically told me my follow-through was starting to hurt opportunities I should be ready for, which was… hard to hear. I guess I keep wanting to say it’s not that bad, but it has caused some real problems.
Do you often feel restless, like it’s hard to sit still?

Not really, I don’t think. I mean, I might shift around in my chair or tap my foot sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I feel like I can’t sit still.

Is that the kind of restless you mean? Because I don’t think that’s a big issue for me.
Did these attention problems start or get noticeably worse after a particular stressful event or major life change?

Um… I wouldn’t say there was one big stressful event that caused it, exactly. It became more noticeable after I moved to Boston after finishing my bachelor’s.

So… I guess it’s been going on for about almost two years now — like, around 1 year and 11 months. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Over the past two weeks, have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless?

Um… not really, no. I mean, I’ve had some frustrating days, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling depressed or hopeless over the past couple weeks.

Is that okay to say? Like, I don’t think that’s been a main thing for me.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot about different things, even when there isn’t an obvious reason to?

Um… I don’t think so, not a lot. I mean, I worry about normal things sometimes, like if I’m behind on something, but I wouldn’t say I’m constantly worrying for no reason.

At least, I don’t think that’s a major thing for me. Is that what you mean?
